original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: In F2[C8] on four registers, prove that diag([g^4]^4) has exact minimum 4 in the rank-one label alphabet D_N([g^s]), s=1..7.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue asks whether a larger register model escapes a three-register obstruction. This package answers the higher 2-power half of the C4 root-lift question: order 8 on four registers, not another three-register abelian word.
bottleneck_link: A three-call root lift would be a shorter bit-primitive word than the diagonal involution product. The rank screen still allows it, so the negative certificate is the obstruction.
stop_rule: Decide length at most 3 versus the four-call diagonal word on this one C8 target. Do not search C16 or a noncommutative extension.
evidence: All 399 label patterns of length 1..3 reduce to a nonzero low-degree rank-one sum or to a degree-4 sum of at most three rank-one matrices. The diagonal four-call word attains the target. An independent meet-in-the-middle over 840 factors finds 0 hits through length 3.
author: Wentao Li
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for the C8 augmentation case split, the exhaustive length-three product check, and the package writeup.

open_questions.question: Does C16, or a specified noncommutative extension of this rank-one label alphabet, admit a three-call word for four involution outputs?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The C4 note asked whether some higher 2-power or noncommutative extension is shorter. C8 is not; the other half is untouched.
open_questions.first_step: Name the group algebra and the target degree, then isolate the cross terms whose valuation equals that degree.
open_questions.blocked_by: Pairwise products of valuation-1 labels land on degree 4 and do not control a degree-8 target. No noncommutative alphabet is fixed here.
